bucketNames.note: The orchestrator does not itself create or name a MinIO bucket. server/src/tests/dbVerification/fileBackupDbIntegration.test.ts (unmodified by this task, per F1-003-P2A §22 item 5's explicit non-authorization) creates its own bucket named `file-backup-review-${Date.now()}`. Bucket-name collision across concurrent runs is structurally impossible regardless: each storage-profile run provisions its own, fully separate, network-isolated MinIO server instance — there is no shared bucket namespace for two runs' buckets to collide in. Collision avoidance for storage is achieved at the container/instance level, not by bucket-name uniqueness alone.

securityImpact.secretGenerationMethod: node:crypto randomBytes — PostgreSQL passwords and MinIO secret keys via generateSecret() (24 random bytes, base64url), MinIO access-key-ids via generateAccessKeyId() (8 random bytes, hex, nmtest-prefixed).
securityImpact.redactionBehavior: lib/redact.ts fully redacts (no partial character reveal) DATABASE_URL passwords and any *_SECRET/*_PASSWORD/*_KEY-shaped environment variable before any logging path; RunSummary objects printed to stdout never contain a raw connection string, password, or access/secret key — only run IDs, container/database names, host ports, and exit codes.
securityImpact.endpointGuardBehavior: Fails closed before any Docker command or migration/test import: rejects any DATABASE_URL/MINIO_ENDPOINT/MINIO_ACCESS_KEY/MINIO_SECRET_KEY already present in the invoking environment; rejects non-loopback hosts; rejects known production hostname patterns; rejects HTTPS MinIO endpoints for the local Docker profile; verifies the constructed database name carries the current run's own identity (not merely a blacklist check).
securityImpact.labelOwnership: Every Docker resource created by this tooling carries com.noramedi.test-runtime=true, com.noramedi.test-run-id, com.noramedi.test-profile, com.noramedi.test-created-at, com.noramedi.test-task=F1-003-P2 — used for precise, label-scoped cleanup and the stale sweeper.
securityImpact.staleCleanupBoundaries: Sweeper only ever touches resources carrying com.noramedi.test-runtime=true and older than the configured TTL (default 4h); no docker system prune, no image deletion, no unlabeled resource ever considered.
securityImpact.commandInjectionResistance: Every Docker invocation uses an argv array via child_process.spawnSync/spawn with shell:false — no string concatenation into a shell. The two shell:true exceptions (Windows npm.cmd/npx.cmd, required because Windows cannot spawn .cmd shims without a shell) pass only fixed internal literal argv elements (script/profile names, 'run', 'prisma', 'migrate', 'deploy') — never externally-supplied or user-controlled text — so no injection surface is introduced by enabling shell:true there.
securityImpact.tempFilePermissions: No secret is ever written to a temp file or a committed .env file — all generated credentials are passed to child processes exclusively via the in-memory env option of child_process.spawn.
securityImpact.externalNetworkBehavior: Zero live external-provider calls occur. The one real external-network-shaped call in the whole verification (the disposable MinIO container) is loopback-bound and network-isolated per run; pre-existing application-level provider mocks (WhatsApp, etc.) already fully stub any other outbound call path, unchanged by this task.
securityImpact.imagePinning: Both images pinned by exact tag with resolved digest recorded in this document; `latest` never used.
securityImpact.supplyChainRisk: Images pulled from official Docker Hub library/postgres and minio/minio repositories only; no third-party or unofficial image reference introduced.
